name: AddrSeq
fullname: Address Sequencer, eight knobs and a start step
summary: Eight bipolar knobs, one a step, with Steps, Start, Reverse and step LEDs.
author: Animatek
about: An eight-step sequencer with one bipolar knob for each step, after Bogaudio's ADDR-SEQ (it was the 5-Step Seq, with the same type). Each rising edge of Clk moves one step on and the last step goes back to the first. Out is the value of the current step, from -64 to +63, and eight LEDs show where it is.
Steps sets the length, 1 to 8 (the steps after it are skipped), Start the step a reset goes to, and Reverse runs the steps backwards, the first going to the last.

Rst works as the G1's own sequencers' does: its edge arms the module and the next clock goes to Start, not to the next step. It starts armed, so the first clock plays Start. With Start 1 it stays in step with a CtrlSeq on the same clock and reset.
usage: Send a clock to Clk and Out to an oscillator's pitch, or to a filter's cutoff.
Set each knob to the value you want for that step, and Steps to the length you want.
Plug a reset into Rst to start the pattern over, from Start.
Plug the same clock and reset into a CtrlSeq (Steps 5, Start 1): the two stay together.
notes: Control rate. A patch saved with the 5-Step Seq keeps its five knobs; Steps, Start and Reverse take their defaults (8 steps, Start 1, forwards), so set Steps to 5 there.

patch_notes.seq5-ctrlseq.pch: One ClkGen clocks an Address Sequencer (Steps 5) and a CtrlSeq; one LFO resets both, keeping them in step.
patch_notes.seq5.pch: ClkGen clocks the Address Sequencer (Steps 5); its knobs set the steps.
